reviews.review: Its great. Combat is great, graphics are good, story is alright, customization is the GOAT, and game performance is demanding. Have a mid to high tier gaming PC as it does not run well on low end. Overall, great game.

8/10, I loved a lot of ♥♥♥♥ about this game, but I also disliked the 'replay gameplay loop' and really couldn't care any less about it. it felt like my time wasn't valued at all and I'm not even guaranteed to see the other bosses or areas I didn't see the first time I played through a map, wtf?? cool guns, classes, abilities, the most worked on bosses were fun (annihilation, alepsis-taura super fun both of them, cube boss too). should be an option to just have a true-playthrough where you get to see every meaningful boss, area, puzzle and interaction. overall difficulty could've gone way up, not with more hp or more dmg, but nerf co-op in some way like creating more meaningful mechanics that interacts with everyone in the party.

TL;DR: I love this game. Buy it. And if you love it as much as I do, grab the DLCs too.

I personally never encountered any bugs or major technical problems while playing. Some people complain about being unable to finish builds even after a lot of farming, but that just wasn’t my experience. At no point did we feel locked out of the story or side quests. Sure, a few puzzles are on the tougher side, but to me those feel more like a test of patience or skill rather than actual design flaws. Playing co-op with a friend, we managed to put together nearly 80% of all archetype setups (including DLC content) and consistently had access to the right rings and amulets to make them work. The only weak spot: pure melee builds don’t hold up well on the higher difficulties.

That aside, the combat is fantastic. Shooting feels precise, impactful, and satisfying. The environments are varied and beautifully designed, dripping with atmosphere and detail. Experimenting with classes is a blast, especially since you can mix two archetypes for unique synergies. Boss fights are an absolute highlight—challenging, diverse, and extremely fun. Exploration never gets dull either, because the worlds are overflowing with secrets.

What makes Remnant II special is how seamlessly it fuses different genres. For me, it’s easily one of the best blends of soulslike challenge, looter-shooter systems, and procedural generation I’ve ever played. This sequel doesn’t just improve on the first game—it elevates the whole concept into something far more refined.

Difficulty & Balance: Unlike many Soulslike-inspired games, the challenge here isn’t artificially punishing. The world scales as you do, keeping fights tense but fair. If something feels overwhelming, you can reroll a campaign or team up with others—especially useful if you’ve got a healer in the group. It’s a clever system that keeps things tough without making progress feel impossible.

Weapons & Builds: The arsenal goes way deeper than it first seems. Weapon mods, especially the unique ones tied to specific guns, completely change how you approach encounters. Combined with class traits, gear choices, and rings/amulets, the amount of buildcrafting variety is huge.

Procedural Worlds & Puzzles: Instead of feeling repetitive like in many other games, the procedural generation here keeps every run fresh. Boss variations, map layouts, and encounter placement constantly shift just enough to surprise you. Puzzles are another clever touch—sometimes straightforward, sometimes cryptic, but always a welcome change of pace from combat.


And then there are the secrets. This is where the game truly shines. Remnant II is stuffed with hidden details, Easter eggs, and mysteries. You simply (literally) cannot uncover everything in a single run. Some secrets are buried so deeply you’ll only find them with outside help—but when you stumble upon one by chance, or finally solve something after hours of curiosity, the payoff is incredible.

That’s why I think it’s a shame this game feels so underrated. For me, Remnant II has become the new standard I measure other games against—and very few are even close. It pulls together so many different elements—challenging combat, buildcrafting, varied worlds, co-op gaming, secrets&puzzles—and delivers a package that feels endlessly rewarding.

To me, Remnant II isn’t just a strong sequel. It’s one of the most creative, surprising, and satisfying games of this generation. (And one you can invest too much time in too easily xD)
